slot.brief: Four statements about NH3 vs other group-15 hydrides (boiling point anomaly, bond angle trend, thermal stability down the group, reducing character) — pick the incorrect one.

stem: Consider the following statements regarding Group 15 hydrides (NH$_3$, PH$_3$, AsH$_3$, SbH$_3$, BiH$_3$). Identify the incorrect statement.
options: NH$_3$ has an exceptionally high boiling point compared to other Group 15 hydrides due to strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
The H–M–H bond angle decreases from NH$_3$ to SbH$_3$ because the bonding orbitals acquire increased p-character as the central atom becomes less electronegative.
The reducing character of the hydrides increases down the group, with BiH$_3$ being the strongest reducing agent.
Thermal stability of the hydrides increases from NH$_3$ to BiH$_3$ because M–H bond dissociation enthalpy increases down the group.

verdicts.working: M–H bond strength decreases down Group 15, so hydride thermal stability decreases—not increases. Thus (C) is incorrect; the other statements are correct.

working:
Thermal stability of Group 15 hydrides decreases from NH$_3$ to BiH$_3$ because the M–H bond strength decreases (bond dissociation enthalpy decreases). Hence statement (C) is incorrect. (A) is correct: NH$_3$ has strong H-bonds leading to a high boiling point. (B) is correct: bond angle decreases due to increased p-character of bonding orbitals (Drago's rule). (D) is correct: reducing character increases down the group.

Independent check: M–H bond strength decreases down Group 15, so hydride thermal stability decreases—not increases. Thus (C) is incorrect; the other statements are correct.
solution: Thermal stability depends on the M–H bond strength. Down Group 15, M–H bond dissociation enthalpy decreases, so hydride thermal stability decreases from NH$_3$ to BiH$_3$; hence statement (D) is incorrect.
